issue: M60 relationship-ontology wave — CLJ-D58 (R10 literal target spelling)
note: ClojureScript names a JavaScript module with a STRING: `(:require ["dayjs" :as dayjs])` puts a `str_lit` where every other libspec puts a `sym_lit`. The libspec reader returned the node's text, so the alias table entry, the `references` edge and (from CLJ-D53) the `imports` edge all carried `"dayjs"` WITH ITS QUOTES — R10's `literal` class, convicted on clojure at 5 sites before this and measured at 8 after CLJ-D53 duplicated them under a second label. The specifier is the string's VALUE, so the value is what is read. This is R10's `literal` class and nothing softer: the target is the whole quoted token, with no name behind it.
